name: Natural Resources Defense Council
mission: The Natural Resources Defense Council's (NRDC) purpose is to safeguard the Earth: its people, its plants and animals and the natural systems on which all life depends. We work to restore the integrity of the elements that sustain life - air, land, and water - and to defend endangered natural places. We seek to establish sustainability and good stewardship of the Earth as central ethical imperatives of human society. NRDC affirms the integral place of human beings in the environment. We strive to protect nature in ways that advance the long-term welfare of present and future generations. We work to foster the fundamental right of all people to have a voice in decisions that affect their environment.
theoryOfChange: The Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) has a published 'Urban Solutions Strategic Plan' which includes a dedicated section titled 'OUR THEORY OF CHANGE'. This strategic plan outlines how NRDC's Urban Solutions program advances strategies to create strong, just, and resilient communities that provide solutions to climate change. The plan details that by 2020, at least 25 urban areas would have deployed integrated, equitable, and replicable climate response strategies as a result of Urban Solutions' tools, technical expertise, and on-site capacity, aiming to reach a tipping point for market-wide adoption of these strategies. The framework focuses on tackling the interconnected challenges of climate change and community vitality by bringing diverse stakeholders together to shape their communities, removing barriers, and working at a large enough scale to reach a transformational 'tipping point'.

rich_narrative.summary: Founded in 1970, the Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC) is an environmental advocacy organization that combines law, science, and policy to protect natural systems and public health [10]. Operating across core areas like <cite id="2">climate change, equity, human health, and nature</cite>, NRDC uses legal action and capacity building to secure environmental policy wins [2]. In FY2024, the organization managed <cite id="10">$193,144,386 in total revenue</cite> to support its environmental operations [10]. NRDC maintains a strong standing with evaluators, earning <cite id="1">an overall score of 99.0/100 from Charity Navigator</cite> [1]. The organization directs <cite id="1">78.6% of its expenses to programs</cite>, matching standard benchmarks for programmatic efficiency [1]. However, NRDC maintains significant financial liquidity with <cite id="1">24.5 months of working capital</cite> in reserves [1]. While its global work spans China, India, and Mexico [2], NRDC operates purely as a general environmental non-profit.
